title: Introduce RBACv2 delegation scopes, KMS region bind, and audit snapshotter
author: Samir Patel
release_notes: Add RBACv2 delegation scopes supporting operator-bounded delegation, KMS region-binding enforcement for tenant CMKs, and an audit snapshotter used for residency attestation and compacting audit streams.
description:
Context and motivation: Customers asked for tighter operator delegation controls and stronger guarantees that tenant data encryption keys are used only in allowed regions. This PR implements three coordinated pieces: 1) RBACv2 delegation scopes (operator->service delegation with explicit allowed-action sets and TTLs), 2) a KMS region bind layer that asserts CMK region affinity at call time and provides soft-fallback telemetry, and 3) an audit snapshotter that periodically compacts residency-relevant audit events into attestable snapshots for offline compliance review.

What this PR changes (high level): - Add 'delegation_scope' primitives to RBACv2 policy model and enforcement paths. Delegation scopes can be minted by platform services and contain permitted role templates, permitted resource filters (by tenant, service, tag), and a TTL. - On the KMS client path add region-binding checks: when a request carries a tenant CMK reference, the region in the KMS metadata must match the tenant's pinned region; violations are rejected unless the tenant has an allowed-mpo (migration-permission) flag. - Audit snapshotter: new background component that streams filtered audit entries (kms operations, rbac delegation events, region-pin violations) and writes time-windowed, signed snapshots to the audit archive bucket for compliance teams. Snapshots include a compact SHA256 index and metadata for proof-of-origin.

Checklist: - [x] Policy model change and DB migration (+ backfill) - [x] Enforcement in auth dispatcher - [x] KMS client region validation with unit tests and a small integration test harness - [x] Audit snapshotter implementation with signing and retention headers - [x] Migration guide and rollout plan in docs/ - [x] E2E smoke in perf-canary for common request paths (no regression in p50/p95) - [x] Security review completed

Files changed (high level): - auth/policy/model.go (add DelegationScope struct, serialization) - auth/dispatcher.go (enforce scoped delegation at decision time) - db/migrations/20250115_add_delegation_scopes.sql (migration + index) - kms/region_bind.go (validation helper, soft-telemetry) - kms/client.go (integrate region check before Encrypt/Decrypt/Sign) - audit/snapshotter/snapshotter.go (streaming, signer) - audit/snapshotter/collector_test.go (tests + fake KMS events) - docs/security/delegation-scopes.md (usage + examples) - helm/values.yaml (feature flag rollout knobs)

Migration notes: - DB migration adds a new table 'delegation_scopes' and a small backfill job that converts historical operator grants into initial scopes with conservative TTLs. The backfill runs as a job that paginates; operator privileges are preserved if the backfill fails but the new enforcement path will treat absent scopes as denied until the backfill completes. - Feature gating: RBACV2_DELEGATION_SCOPES=off by default for 48 hours; helm chart exposes a gradual rollout percentage knob. - KMS region bind is opt-in via TENANT_REGION_BIND=true; customer-managed tenants are evaluated first. Operators can enable strict mode (reject on mismatch) or lax mode (record telemetry and attach an 'allowlist' bypass) during gradual rollout.

Performance and safety: - Added microbenchmarks for dispatcher policy checks; p50 overhead is ~0.6ms median on our canaries. - Snapshotter uses streaming batches with a 10s flush window and is backpressure-aware. - Added circuit-breaker and retry policies around KMS validation to avoid increasing latencies on transient KMS errors.

Tests and CI: - Unit tests cover policy model serialization, delegation TTL enforcement, KMS region mismatch handling, and snapshot integrity verification. - Integration tests included in 'internal/integration/kms_region_bind_test' exercising actual mocked KMS endpoints. - CI pipeline: lint -> unit tests -> integration (docker fixtures) -> security-scan. One flaky integration test was stabilized (collector_test.go) after addressing race on the fake-queue.

Review conversation summary: - Linnea Huang: "Can delegation scopes be limited to a subset of role templates rather than arbitrary roles? Also we need a deterministic deny precedence when both a direct role and a scope exist." Author reply: "Yes — scopes carry an explicit 'allowed_role_templates' list, and enforcement orders direct role grants before scopes; added unit tests to assert precedence." - Carlos Mendes: "Region bind should surface a clear metric and a tenant-level diagnostic header so SRE can triage false positives." Author reply: "Added metrics kms.region_bind.violation_count and a X-Tenant-Region-Check header emitted on requests that fail; updated observability docs." - Priya Nair (security): "Ensure KMS checks can't be bypassed by service-account impersonation." Author reply: "Added an operator-scope whitelist that requires two-step approval to list, enforced from operator-mgmt service; documented the audit trail for approvals." - Requested change: stabilize snapshot signer concurrency — addressed in follow-up commit which serializes signing per-window and reuses signer instances. - Final approvals: Linnea (approved), Priya (approved), Carlos (approved).

Merge details: - Merge method: squash and merge - Merge commit: "squash: rbacv2: delegation scopes + kms region bind + audit snapshotter" - Post-merge hooks: triggered migration backfill job and rolled out the feature gate to 10% of traffic for 24h, then 100% after monitoring window.

Operational playbook (short): - If region-bind violations spike: check the tenant's pinned_region in tenant-service and the KMS key metadata map; use /admin/diagnostics/region-bind to gather failing traces. - To rollback: flip TENANT_REGION_BIND=false and RBACV2_DELEGATION_SCOPES=off via console; the dispatcher will fall back to legacy grants for 5 minutes while the old path drains. - Snapshot issues: snapshots are stored under gs://redwood-audit-snapshots/{yyyy}/{mm}/{tenant}/; signed index included. Compliance can fetch using signed URLs and validate SHA256 indexes.

Related work and follow-ups: - Follow-up tasks added to Linear: ENG-2540 (UI for delegation scope creation), ENG-2541 (OPA linter rule for scopes), SEC-1104 (KMS provider integration test with external HSM).
